finding.claim: The /users endpoint takes the tenant identifier (org) from a client-supplied query parameter. It performs no authentication or check that the caller belongs to that org. Any caller can list the id and name of users in any organization by changing ?org=. This is an IDOR / broken tenant isolation. It is only exploitable if no auth or tenancy middleware exists outside this file. No such middleware is visible, and req.pg is also not set here, so the app is presumably wired up elsewhere.
finding.source: req.query.org (attacker-controlled HTTP query parameter, GET /users?org=<victim org>)
finding.sink: req.pg.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1") returning rows to the caller via res.json

trace.note: Route registered with no auth middleware or per-route authorization check
req.query.org is passed directly as the org filter. It is not compared with an authenticated principal's org.
Result rows are returned to the requester unfiltered

finding.guards_checked: The SQL is parameterized ($1), so there is no SQL injection. There is no app.use() auth, session or org-scoping middleware in db.js, and it is the only file in the directory. Also checked and not exploitable: /file, whose path.resolve + startsWith(ROOT + path.sep) check blocks traversal (a non-string name only causes a thrown error and a 500), and /count, whose execFile call uses fixed arguments with no user input.

verdict.guard_found: none (the SQL at db.js:9 is parameterized, which stops SQL injection but not cross-tenant access; no auth or tenancy middleware exists in db.js, the only file in the directory)
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: db.js:8-10 register /users with no auth and pass req.query.org straight into the query. However, nothing in db.js ever sets req.pg, so as written the handler throws a TypeError at db.js:9 and never returns data. Whether it is exploitable depends on external wiring and on whether the endpoint is meant to be public, and neither can be determined from this directory.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none (only a parameterized query, which stops SQL injection but not cross-tenant access)
verdict_facts.reason: db.js:9 filters users by the client-supplied req.query.org and db.js:10 returns the rows, with no check at db.js:8-10 that the caller (req.user or similar) belongs to that org, so any HTTP client can read any org's user ids and names.
